title: K-flat complexes and stalks at points of a ringed site
statement: Let $C$ be a site small in the coefficient universe [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], let $R$ be a sheaf of commutative rings on $C$, and let $K^\bullet$ be a cochain complex of sheaves of $R$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. A point means a geometric morphism $p:\mathbf{Set}\to\operatorname{Sh}(C)$ [def-trf-geometric-morphism]. Put $R_p=p^{-1}R$ and $K_p^\bullet=p^{-1}K^\bullet$ termwise, with the $R_p$-module action induced by applying $p^{-1}$ to the action and using its finite-product comparison. If $K^\bullet$ is K-flat [def-pc-kflat-complex], then $K_p^\bullet$ is K-flat as a complex of $R_p$-modules [def-pc-module-kflat-complex] for every point $p$. Conversely, suppose there is a set-indexed family $(p_i)_{i\in I}$ of points whose inverse images jointly reflect isomorphisms of sheaves of sets. If $K_{p_i}^\bullet$ is K-flat over $R_{p_i}$ for every $i$, then $K^\bullet$ is K-flat. No flatness assumption on the individual terms and no boundedness assumption is imposed.

proof.text: The normalized module stalk functor is exact and commutes with signed unbounded total tensor. A conservative family on set sheaves detects acyclicity of module complexes, using reflection on the map from each homology to zero.

Choose P→K from the reduced flat resolution, with P K-flat on the site and with K-flat stalk. If K is K-flat, its cone E is K-flat by the independent-coefficient cone theorem and is acyclic by the quasi-isomorphism cone criterion.

An acyclic K-flat E tensors acyclically with every source complex. For each finitely presented stalk module M, the universal matrix retract lemma, exact stalks and tensor compatibility imply that E_p tensor M[0] is acyclic. The ordinary module finite-presentation criterion makes E_p K-flat.

Additive module inverse image commutes with the mapping cone, so E_p is the cone of P_p→K_p. In the homotopy category the quasi-isomorphism K-flat property is triangulated and closed under two-out-of-three. Since P_p and E_p are K-flat, K_p is K-flat.

Conversely, for each acyclic source F, exact stalks make F_p acyclic. K-flat K_p makes its tensor with F_p acyclic. Tensor comparison identifies these with stalks of F tensor K, and conservative-family acyclicity detection gives source acyclicity. This holds for every F and proves K-flatness, including an empty conservative family.

reviewed_lean.note: I checked the item theorem CochainComplex.ringedSite_kFlat_stalk_criterion clause by clause against the node and Stacks 0DEN. The site uses EssentiallySmall.{w} with a Precoverage and IsSiteForCoverings, R is a sheaf of commutative rings, K is an unbounded ℤ-complex in ringedSiteModules.{w} (w is the module universe). Points are GeometricMorphism (Type w) (Sheaf (Type w)). Both directions use the recorded IsKFlatIndependentCoefficients and MorphismProperty.kFlat predicates. The converse uses JointlyReflectIsomorphisms over a free index universe t with no Nonempty, the same form as lem-trf-point-family-conservative. There are no flatness, boundedness or finite-limit hypotheses. The new def-sfb-ringed-site-point (RingedSitePoint) is real data: because the point's inverse image preserves finite limits, its conditions on all test sheaves force the transported finite-product operations, and naturality fixes the maps. So the data are unique up to unique iso, quantifying over every presentation equals the natural statement, and the existence theorem is true. I found no existing equivalent in Mathlib Sites.Point, AlgebraicInverseImage, constant-coefficient point evaluation or topological stalks. Both statement fields are verbatim in their files. Imports match the proof dependencies with Lean records. Docstrings give sources, blueprint IDs and all six proof steps.
